title: Extraction and Contact
premise: Marguerite Brightwater, a deniable fixer for a shadow embassy, is tasked with quietly retrieving a passenger manifest from Flight 4471 before it lands. Mid-flight, every digital and paper record of the aircraft evaporates across three governments' databases, and Marguerite realizes someone inside his own network is erasing the plane—and the forty-one people aboard—to protect a pre-summit arms deal. Hunting the truth through Vienna, Istanbul, and Geneva, he is hunted in turn by an assassin who once trained beside him, while the only witness, a flight attendant smuggled off the tarmac, forces him to choose between his invisibility and his conscience. In the end, Marguerite burns his own cover to deliver the manifest to the summit floor, exposing the deal at the cost of his employer's protection; the assassin, revealed as the operation's true architect, dies by his own protocol, and Marguerite walks away stateless but finally belonging to himself.
about_author: Dominic Zhou is a former logistics consultant who spent a decade shuttling between diplomatic back channels in Central Europe before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose names appear on no official list, drawing on the bureaucratic twilight he once inhabited.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Marguerite Brightwater receives a routine assignment: retrieve a passenger manifest from Flight 4471 before it lands in Vienna. His POV establishes his meticulous invisibility—no fixed address, three passports, no reflection in any system. The emotional beat is quiet pride in being unrecorded, which the chapter subtly frames as loneliness.

chapters.title: Forty-One Names
chapters.summary: At the airport, Marguerite copies the manifest by hand, noting one anomaly: a name flagged in red that his handler refuses to explain. A flight attendant, Ilse Marchetti, catches him photographing documents. His POV; the beat is unease—the first crack in a routine he trusted.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: While the plane is still airborne, every record of Flight 4471 vanishes: flight plans, radar archives, the manifest itself. Marguerite's own copies become the only evidence the aircraft exists. His POV, escalating dread as he realizes the erasure required access no outsider possesses.

chapters.title: The Embassy That Isn't
chapters.summary: Marguerite reports to his handler, Voss, at the unmarked townhouse that serves as his embassy. Voss orders him to destroy his copies and stand down. Marguerite obeys outwardly but keeps one page hidden. His POV; the beat is the first act of disobedience in a career built on compliance.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Ilse Marchetti contacts Marguerite: she was scheduled on 4471 but pulled at the last minute, and her crewmates are now officially never employed. She wants answers; he wants her silence. Alternating POV begins. The beat is two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Red Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite traces the flagged passenger: Anton Rezek, a mid-level arms broker tied to a weapons package moving through three governments ahead of next week's summit. His POV; the beat is the case expanding from oddity to conspiracy.

chapters.title: A Professional Courtesy
chapters.summary: In Istanbul, Marguerite meets the assassin Kade—a former colleague from his training days—now working for unknown principals, who warns him off with genuine regret. Kade's POV reveals he was ordered to erase everyone connected to the flight. The beat is old friendship weaponized.

chapters.title: What the Radar Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilse and Marguerite find a retired air traffic controller whose personal logs show 4471 never transmitted a landing signal—it went dark over the Carpathians. His POV interleaved with hers; the beat is grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Downed Plane
chapters.summary: A trek to a remote crash site confirms wreckage consistent with 4471, already stripped of identifying parts. Marguerite realizes the passengers may have been removed before impact. His POV; the beat is horror shifting toward fury.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite maps the cover-up: each government erased its own slice of records, none admitting the whole. He identifies the coordination point—a private security firm feeding all three. His POV; the beat is cold clarity, the thriller's machinery laid bare.

chapters.title: Safe House
chapters.summary: Kade finds Ilse first; Marguerite extracts her minutes before the safe house burns. Wounded, they hide in a church hostel in Bratislava. Alternating POV; the beat is forced intimacy between two people with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss offers Marguerite restoration of his records and protection if he surrenders Ilse and the manifest page. Marguerite understands his own employers are inside the perimeter of the plot. His POV; the beat is betrayal crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Manifest Page
chapters.summary: Ilse decodes the red-flagged annotation: Rezek was traveling under diplomatic cover arranged by the security firm, meaning the arms deal has official fingerprints. Her POV; the beat is a civilian outthinking the professionals.

chapters.title: Old Training Ground
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Kade in an abandoned airfield where they once trained, trying to turn him. Kade admits he executed the ground team but claims he doesn't know who gave the order—or where the passengers went. His POV; the beat is loyalty cracking under doubt.

chapters.title: Forty-One Chairs
chapters.summary: Following a supply trail, they find a decommissioned detention facility where the passengers were held—and evidence most were moved again days ago, alive. Marguerite's POV; the beat is hope rekindled, raising stakes: this is now a rescue.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: The security firm is selling the hostages' silence individually—witnesses to the arms shipment—before the summit convenes. Ilse infiltrates the auction's logistics as contract crew. Her POV; the beat is terror managed through competence.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Voss declares Marguerite compromised; his passports begin dying one by one, his accounts freezing in real time. For the first time, he is fully visible and fully alone. His POV; the beat is identity stripped to its foundation—the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Kade's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to kill both of them, Kade instead delivers the name of his principal: the deputy director inside Marguerite's own embassy, who orchestrated the erasure to protect the summit deal. His POV ends with him accepting he won't survive the week. The beat is redemption priced in blood.

chapters.title: Geneva, Night Before
chapters.summary: With forged credentials from Ilse's airline contacts, Marguerite prepares to breach the summit's secure annex where the remaining witnesses are held. They admit this may be their last night. Alternating POV; the beat is quiet love declared without ceremony.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Marguerite breaches the annex, frees eleven surviving passengers, and confronts the deputy director, recording his confession as Kade holds off the response team and falls. His POV; the climax beat is a man choosing justice outside the law at maximum cost.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: Marguerite walks the recording and manifest into the summit plenum, burning his last cover, and hands everything to journalists and delegates simultaneously so it cannot be buried. His POV; the beat is triumph inseparable from exile.

chapters.title: Belonging to Himself
chapters.summary: Weeks later: inquiries launched, arrests made, the shadow embassy quietly dissolved. Ilse and Marguerite meet in a small coastal town where, for the first time, he uses his real name aloud. Shared final POV; the resolution beat is identity reclaimed—not granted by any state, but chosen.
